newsitem.title: USA: US mulls options for curbing Canada wheat imports.
newsitem.headline: US mulls options for curbing Canada wheat imports.

text.p: The United States is looking at options for curbing wheat imports from Canada, including a possible investigation into whether Canada is unfairly "dumping" discounted wheat in the U.S. market, a top U.S. official said Thursday.

Speaking with reporters after meeting with northern state senators, U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said "the level of concern is very high in the administration" about the recent increase in wheat imports from Canada.
"We're looking at options right now" for reducing the level of imports, Glickman said. But he said no decision on any course of action had been made in the meeting with the lawmakers.

U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said the United States was also concerned about the amount of market access that Canada provides for wheat imports from the United States. She noted that current U.S. wheat shipments to Canada are "quite limited."

In the fall of 1994 the United States imposed a one-year, 1.5 million ton quota on imports of wheat from Canada. But Barshefsky acknowledged Thursday there was no current agreement limiting the amount of wheat coming into the United States from Canada.

She denied that the administration was "stymied" over what to do about the imports, which anger Northern Plains wheat producers who feel that Canada is encroaching on their market. Barshefsky said the Commerce Department would look at whether a dumping investigation is in order. Barshefsky said the Commerce Department would meet with U.S. wheat producers to decide whether to pursue a dumping investigation with Canada. Commerce Secretary William Daley will also raise the issue with the Canadians in meetings next week, lawmakers said.
